annotator_prompt.name: completed_pickups
annotator_prompt.description: In goals requesting two ordered container pickups, the first container was lifted, then lowered and released, concealing its cube again. The existing uncovered_scene and button_pressed fields did not preserve that completed pickup, so the policy returned to the first container instead of selecting the second. This breaks SUFFICIENCY. Add a count of completed pickups in the goal's requested order, initially 0. Increment once when the next required container has actually been lifted while grasped to approximately z=0.20, exposing its cube; do not increment on grasp closure or selection of a lift waypoint. Retain the count through lowering, release, and retreat. In the supplied two-pickup trajectories it becomes 1 at the observation of the first completed lift and remains 1 throughout the second approach, grasp, and commanded lift. In trajectories ending with the first lift command, it remains 0 because no completed lift has yet been observed. Example value: 1.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: completed_pickups
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: After the first requested container was returned to the table, its cube was hidden again and the empty hand did not reveal that the pickup had already occurred. With only the initial scene and button flag, the policy repeated the first pickup, breaking SUFFICIENCY. Initialize completed_pickups to 0. Read the ordered container colors directly from the goal. Increment the incoming count once only when this cycle's motion frames show the container for the next uncompleted requested color being lifted with a closed grasp, reaching approximately z=0.20 and exposing the corresponding cube. Use the incoming count to identify which pickup qualifies; a continued hold or lowering of an already counted container must not increment it again. Do not increment merely because fingers closed or a lift is now commanded. Otherwise copy the incoming value, including through release and retreat. Example: write 1 upon observing the first successful lift, and retain 1 while approaching and grasping the second container.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
Failures occurred in three related situations. At the button, the policy treated an approximately reached hover as the true button center and copied the measured TCP x,y into closing and pressing commands, retaining an approach error greater than 1 cm. At a target-container approach, it estimated a top center and yaw directly from the perspective image, producing the wrong world grasp pose. In ordered two-pickup goals, the unconditional instruction to keep holding the first container prevented release; after release the absence of progress handling caused repeated targeting of the first container or an incorrect retreat height. These are SUFFICIENCY failures in the action rules; pickup progress additionally requires the new completed_pickups memory.

Keep the existing button-contact detection, press heights, and pre/post-press branching, but explicitly separate hover-arrival tolerance from target-coordinate estimation. Arrival tolerance only decides whether the next operation is closing or pressing. For every button hover, closing, pressing, and retraction command, estimate the circular button's actual world center from calibrated current imagery at its physical height. Never substitute the measured hover TCP x,y for that center. In particular, closing at hover commands the re-estimated center at z=0.15, and pressing commands that center at z=0.0075 with fingers closed. Use the existing nonidentical-waypoint safeguard for gripper-only changes.

Make container pose reconstruction explicit. Associate containers with the requested cube locations in uncovered_scene using calibrated world geometry, not raw image centroid overlap. Reconstruct the visible square top's corners by intersecting calibrated camera rays with its top/grasp plane, approximately z=0.0633–0.0634. Compute the world-plane center and derive yaw from reconstructed world-plane edges, not image-plane slopes. Choose the equivalent square-aligned yaw closest to zero. Refine with current wrist geometry while accounting for the offset between optical center and TCP projection. Use this estimated container center for both its z=0.20 open-hand hover and its grasp-height descent with closure, rather than copying an offset realized hover position.

Replace the unconditional instruction to keep holding every lifted container with ordered-goal handling. Read the requested color order from the goal; with an empty hand, completed_pickups selects the next uncompleted color. Current observed lift completion counts immediately for action selection, even though its updated memory is only carried into the next cycle. A closed grasp at approximately z=0.0634 still requires lifting to z=0.20 over the grasp center, retaining its square-aligned yaw and closed grip. Do not regard a commanded lift as completed.

When a required container has visibly reached approximately z=0.20 in a closed grasp and another requested pickup remains, lower that held container at the current measured x,y to z=0.07, preserving the current orientation, and open on arrival. This returns the container over its original cube; retain pickup completion even when the cube is concealed again. This release rule takes priority over approaching the next target. With open fingers low over the returned container, retract vertically to approximately z=0.145, preserving current x,y and orientation and keeping the gripper open. This specific release-clearance rule replaces the generic z=0.20 fallback in that situation and takes priority over any grasp rule. Once the open hand has reached that clearance height, move directly to the next requested container's z=0.20 hover using completed_pickups and uncovered_scene. If already at that next container's hover, descend to its reconstructed grasp center and close; after grasping, lift it closed to z=0.20. Do not revisit the previously completed container or repeat the button press. When the last requested pickup is lifted, retain the closed grasp rather than returning or releasing it. Preserve the existing no-step recovery and nonidentical-waypoint safeguards; do not introduce purposeless waits.

fields.name: uncovered_scene
fields.description: With empty memory, store the label of the first current execution frame showing the exposed colored cubes. Thereafter copy the incoming label unchanged, including after containers appear. Use the retained image to identify where the cube named by the goal was concealed. e.g. "E0"
fields.annotation: Store the first execution frame showing the colored cubes before containers conceal them. Retain this same label throughout the episode. This preserves the association between the instructed cube color and the subsequently covering container, not a fixed container rank or image-side choice. In all supplied episodes this is E0. e.g. "E0"

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: With empty memory initialize false. Set true when the current motion frames and robot state show the closed fingers have descended onto the circular button and reached contact, with TCP near z=0.024 m over its center. Otherwise copy the incoming value. Never set true merely because containers appeared, the fingers closed at hover height, or a downward press is being commanded. Once true, retain true. e.g. false

Contact ends with the TCP approximately 0.024 m above the table even though the commanded press height is 0.0075 m. Thus this field is false at cycles 1–3 and true at cycles 4–8 in every supplied episode. Record observed completion, not the selection of a future pressing waypoint. e.g. false

fields.annotation: The number of pickups completed in the goal's requested order. Initialize to 0. Increment once when the cycle shows the next required container actually lifted in a closed grasp to approximately z=0.20, exposing its cube. Do not increment on grasp closure or on selection of a lift waypoint. A continued hold or lowering of an already counted container does not count again. Retain the count through return, release, and retreat, even when the cube becomes concealed again. e.g. 1

texts.action:
Begin with the open hand high above the table and empty memory. Identify the circular gray button on its square base and the cube color specified by the goal. Use calibrated camera geometry, not image-side labels, to estimate world coordinates. The front image's right is world +y. Recover object centers using their physical heights rather than projecting elevated top faces onto the table. The retained uncovered_scene supplies the cube-to-container association after the cubes disappear; compare its cube locations with the current containers, allowing for their top-face height and perspective. Extra containers are distractors. Do not infer that container appearance means the button has been pressed.

Apply the following rules to the observed situation. Use current contact evidence together with incoming button_pressed to recognize that the press has occurred; the outgoing memory is not a prerequisite for recognizing current contact. Likewise, use incoming completed_pickups together with any qualifying lift completion observed this cycle to determine the number of completed pickups for action selection. A commanded lift is not a completed pickup. Read the requested color order from the goal; with an empty hand, select the next uncompleted color. Never repeat a completed pickup or the completed button press.

Button-hover arrival tolerance determines which operation is next, not the button's coordinates. For every button approach, closing, pressing, opening, and retraction command, reconstruct the circular button's actual world center from calibrated current imagery at its physical height. Never substitute the measured hover TCP x,y for that center. Closing at hover uses that center at z=0.15; pressing uses that center at z=0.0075. Preserve the nonidentical-waypoint safeguard for gripper-only changes.

Before pressing: if the hand is not at the button hover, command [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper open. Treat an approach ending within roughly 1.5 cm horizontally and 1 cm vertically as arrival. If at this hover with open fingers, command the same nominal hover with gripper closed. If at hover with closed fingers and button_pressed is false, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper closed. Do not repeatedly drive downward when the fingers have contacted the button: the realized TCP may stop near z=0.024 rather than the commanded height.

After observed button contact, or with button_pressed true: if still low over the button, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0], keeping the gripper closed. At the button hover with closed fingers, open the gripper at that nominal hover. At the button hover with open fingers, move directly to the target-container hover, not back down onto the button.

The target is the container covering the next uncompleted requested color in uncovered_scene. Associate the remembered cube locations with current containers using calibrated world coordinates, not raw image-centroid overlap. Reconstruct the visible square top's corners by intersecting calibrated camera rays with its top/grasp plane, approximately z=0.0633–0.0634. Compute the world-plane center from these corners and derive yaw from the reconstructed world-plane edges, not image-plane slopes. Choose a downward orientation [3.1416, 0, yaw] aligned with opposing grasp faces, using the equivalent square-aligned yaw closest to zero. Refine the estimate with current wrist geometry, distinguishing the optical center from the TCP projection. Use this reconstructed container center for both the open-hand hover [target_x, target_y, 0.20, 3.1416, 0, yaw] and the descent to z approximately 0.0634 with closure on arrival. When already at the target hover with open fingers, descend rather than repeating the hover. Do not copy an offset realized hover position into the grasp command or substitute the remembered cube's image centroid for the elevated container's current top center. Apply the held-container return and release-clearance rules before any next-target approach or grasp.

When the fingers have closed around the target at grasp height, typically leaving about 0.018 m on each finger, lift to z=0.20 over the same grasp center with the same yaw and gripper closed. Do not treat selection of this waypoint as completion.

When the required container has actually reached approximately z=0.20 in a closed grasp and another requested pickup remains, return it over its original cube: command the current measured x,y at z=0.07, preserving the current orientation, and open on arrival. This return-and-release rule takes priority over approaching the next target. Preserve the completed pickup count even when the returned container conceals its cube.

With open fingers low over a returned, already completed container, retract vertically to approximately z=0.145 at the current x,y and orientation, keeping the gripper open. This release-clearance rule takes priority over grasp rules and the generic hover fallback. Once at this clearance height, move directly to the next uncompleted container's z=0.20 hover. Then descend, close, and lift according to the target rules. When the last requested pickup has actually been lifted, retain the closed grasp; do not return or release it. Never try to grasp a revealed cube.

For commands that only change the gripper, use the nominal hover target if it differs from the measured TCP by at least 2 mm. Otherwise add a 3 mm upward displacement so the waypoint is not identical to the current pose. Small execution errors do not imply a new task stage or require replaying an already completed press.

If alignment is uncertain, use the retained scene and current wrist/front geometry to refine the relevant object's location and make a corrective open-hand hover motion before descending. If a commanded motion explicitly executed no steps, preserve memory and retry the applicable rule with a reachable, nonidentical waypoint. For an otherwise unmatched situation, safely raise the hand vertically to the relevant hover height, preserving a held object's closed grip, then reapply these observation-based rules. Do not wait without a specific observable purpose.

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: With empty memory initialize to 0. Read the requested color order from the goal. Increment the incoming count once when this cycle's motion frames show the container for the next uncompleted requested color being lifted in a closed grasp to approximately z=0.20 and exposing its cube. Use the incoming count to identify which pickup qualifies. Do not count continued holding or lowering of an already completed pickup, grasp closure alone, or a lift that is only being commanded. Otherwise copy the incoming value, including through return, release, and retreat. e.g. 1
